cards.back: $$\mathbf{A}\cdot\mathbf{B}=|\mathbf{A}||\mathbf{B}|\cos\theta_{AB}=A_xB_x+A_yB_y+A_zB_z$$It is a scalar, and zero when the vectors are perpendicular.

cards.front: Magnitude of the cross product, and its direction?
cards.back: $$|\mathbf{A}\times\mathbf{B}|=|\mathbf{A}||\mathbf{B}|\sin\theta_{AB}$$Perpendicular to both, by the right-hand rule. Zero when the vectors are parallel.
$$\mathbf{A}\times\mathbf{B}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{\mathbf{x}}&\hat{\mathbf{y}}&\hat{\mathbf{z}}\\A_x&A_y&A_z\\B_x&B_y&B_z\end{vmatrix}$$
$\hat{\mathbf{z}}$, $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$. Each set is right-handed in the order $(x,y,z)$, $(r,\phi,z)$, $(R,\theta,\phi)$.
$$r=\sqrt{x^2+y^2},\qquad \phi=\tan^{-1}\frac{y}{x},\qquad z=z$$Pick the quadrant of $\phi$ from the signs of $x$ and $y$.
$$x=R\sin\theta\cos\phi,\quad y=R\sin\theta\sin\phi,\quad z=R\cos\theta$$

cards.front: Ranges of $\theta$ and $\phi$ in spherical coordinates?
cards.back: $0\le\theta\le\pi$, measured down from the $+z$ axis. $0\le\phi<2\pi$, measured from the $+x$ axis in the $xy$-plane.

cards.front: Why can't you add $\hat{\mathbf{r}}$ components at two different points?
cards.back: $\hat{\mathbf{r}}$, $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$, $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}$ point in different directions at different points. Convert to Cartesian first.
$$d\mathbf{l}=\hat{\mathbf{r}}\,dr+\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}\,r\,d\phi+\hat{\mathbf{z}}\,dz$$

cards.front: Differential volume in cylindrical and spherical coordinates?
cards.back: $$dV=r\,dr\,d\phi\,dz,\qquad dV=R^2\sin\theta\,dR\,d\theta\,d\phi$$

cards.front: Differential area on a sphere of radius $R$?
cards.back: $$d\mathbf{s}=\hat{\mathbf{R}}\,R^2\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\phi$$

cards.front: What does the gradient $\nabla V$ tell you?
cards.back: The direction in which $V$ increases fastest, with magnitude equal to that rate. It is perpendicular to surfaces of constant $V$.
$$\nabla V=\hat{\mathbf{x}}\frac{\partial V}{\partial x}+\hat{\mathbf{y}}\frac{\partial V}{\partial y}+\hat{\mathbf{z}}\frac{\partial V}{\partial z}$$

cards.front: Directional derivative of $V$ along unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{a}}$?
cards.back: $$\frac{dV}{dl}=\nabla V\cdot\hat{\mathbf{a}}$$
Net outward flux per unit volume at a point. Positive at a source, negative at a sink, zero where flux in equals flux out.
$$\nabla\cdot\mathbf{A}=\frac{\partial A_x}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial A_y}{\partial y}+\frac{\partial A_z}{\partial z}$$
$$\nabla\cdot\mathbf{A}=\frac{1}{r}\frac{\partial(rA_r)}{\partial r}+\frac{1}{r}\frac{\partial A_\phi}{\partial\phi}+\frac{\partial A_z}{\partial z}$$
$$\int_V\nabla\cdot\mathbf{A}\,dV=\oint_S\mathbf{A}\cdot d\mathbf{s}$$
Circulation per unit area: how much the field swirls around a point. A small paddle wheel in the field spins about the curl's direction.
$$\nabla\times\mathbf{A}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{\mathbf{x}}&\hat{\mathbf{y}}&\hat{\mathbf{z}}\\\partial_x&\partial_y&\partial_z\\A_x&A_y&A_z\end{vmatrix}$$
$$\int_S(\nabla\times\mathbf{A})\cdot d\mathbf{s}=\oint_C\mathbf{A}\cdot d\mathbf{l}$$$C$ bounds $S$; walk $C$ so the right-hand rule gives the direction of $d\mathbf{s}$.

cards.front: Distance vector from point $P_1$ to point $P_2$?
cards.back: $$\mathbf{R}_{12}=\mathbf{R}_2-\mathbf{R}_1=\hat{\mathbf{x}}(x_2-x_1)+\hat{\mathbf{y}}(y_2-y_1)+\hat{\mathbf{z}}(z_2-z_1)$$Always from the first point to the second.
